items.stem: What basic principle allows radar to detect a distant object?

options.text: It transmits electromagnetic energy and measures the reflected echo
options.rationale: Correct: radar times and measures reflected signals.

options.text: It listens only to sound waves from the object
options.rationale: Radar uses electromagnetic waves, not sound.

options.text: It requires physical contact with the object
options.rationale: Radar is a remote, non-contact sensing method.

options.text: It works only in bright daylight
options.rationale: Radar does not depend on visible light.

items.explanation: Correct: radar times and measures reflected signals.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about comparing sensor modalities are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Infrared sensors can detect heat signatures at night
options.rationale: Correct: IR senses thermal emission regardless of daylight.

options.text: Radar can operate through many weather conditions that limit optical sensors
options.rationale: Correct: radar penetrates cloud and darkness better than optical.

options.text: Optical cameras see perfectly through thick fog
Lidar and radar are identical in every way
options.rationale: They use different wavelengths and have different strengths.

items.explanation: Correct: IR senses thermal emission regardless of daylight.

items.stem: Why is sensor fusion often used in complex sensing systems?

options.text: Combining sensors gives a more complete and reliable picture than any one alone
options.rationale: Correct: fusion leverages complementary sensor strengths.

options.text: Because one sensor is always perfect
options.rationale: No single sensor is ideal in all conditions.

options.text: Because fusion removes the need for processing
Because more sensors always cost nothing
options.rationale: Added sensors add cost and complexity.

items.explanation: Correct: fusion leverages complementary sensor strengths.
